description.p: PenguinCAD is an open-source parametric solid modeller that works the way Fusion 360 does: a feature timeline you can roll back, a constrained sketcher that drives it, a marking menu under the right mouse button, and the same shortcut keys. It is built on the OpenCASCADE geometry kernel.
It is early software. Today it can:

ul.li: Save and reopen designs as human-readable .pcad files, timeline and parameters included
Sketch lines, rectangles, circles, arcs, splines and more, with constraints and driving dimensions
Extrude, revolve, sweep and loft, joining, cutting or intersecting with existing bodies
Fillet, chamfer, shell, pattern and mirror
Drive every dimension from named parameters and unit-checked expressions
Import and export STEP, and export STL and OBJ

description.p: Assemblies and 2D drawings are not available yet. The project is looking for contributors.

description.p: PenguinCAD now installs from its own signed Flatpak repository, so it appears in GNOME Software and KDE Discover and updates like any other app. Designs open in PenguinCAD when double-clicked.
If you installed 0.1.0 from the downloaded file, remove it once and install again from the website; from then on it updates itself.

ul.li: Sketching with constraints and driving dimensions
Extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, fillet, chamfer, shell, patterns and mirror
Saving and opening designs as .pcad files
Fusion 360's marking menu, navigation and shortcut keys
STEP import and export; STL and OBJ export
